title: Pivot lst to git-backed multi-vault Markdown tooling
description:
## Context

The desired product direction for `lst` is a fast, local-first Markdown tool for quickly creating and updating notes/lists, finding information quickly, and using a Tauri mobile app to work across devices.

The existing CRDT/encrypted relay sync architecture is more complex than the current need. Git is good enough as the primary sync substrate for Markdown vaults and is easier to inspect, repair, and delegate to agents.

The shared wiki (`~/wiki`) should be treated as one target Markdown vault, not the whole product. `lst` should support multiple vaults: personal notes/lists, wiki, work notes, project-specific Markdown stores, etc.

## Decision direction

Build on top of the existing `lst` repository instead of starting from scratch, but simplify the architecture aggressively:

- Keep: CLI, Markdown storage, config/schema, note/list UX, Tauri mobile/desktop surfaces, theme/UI investment.
- Demote/freeze: CRDT sync, zero-knowledge server, custom sync daemon as the default path.
- Add: explicit vault abstraction, git-backed sync commands, better search/find, wiki lint/conventions as vault-specific tooling.

If current code is too tangled, create new clean crates inside the repo (for example `lst-vault`) rather than creating a new repository.

## Desired outcome

`lst` becomes a git-backed, multi-vault Markdown notes/lists tool with excellent CLI, search, and mobile editing. Wiki/OKF support becomes a vault profile layered on top of the generic vault model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Child issues exist for architecture decision/docs, vault abstraction, git sync, search/find, wiki vault profile, mobile implications, and CRDT/server deprecation plan.
- [ ] The direction is documented before implementation.
- [ ] Existing `lst-xadf` OKF/wiki issues are linked or reconciled with the vault direction.
- [ ] No child issue requires continuing CRDT/server sync as the default path.
- [ ] The migration path preserves current CLI usefulness while enabling a cleaner core.

## Proof of success

A user can configure at least two local Markdown vaults, create/update notes and lists in either vault, search across a chosen vault, and sync via git without running `lst-server` or `lst-syncd`.

title: Document the git-backed vault architecture decision
description:
## What to do

Write an architecture/design note that records the pivot from CRDT/server-first sync to git-backed multi-vault Markdown tooling.

## Include

- Why building on the existing `lst` repo is preferred over starting from scratch.
- What stays: CLI, Markdown note/list commands, config/schema, Tauri apps, theme/UI work.
- What is demoted or frozen: CRDT sync, encrypted relay server, default sync daemon path.
- The new core abstraction: a `Vault` is a local Markdown directory with optional profile/conventions and optional git sync.
- The wiki is one vault/profile, not the entire product.
- The migration strategy: build a clean vault layer in the repo, then move CLI/mobile features onto it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Design note exists in `docs/` and is linked from README or a docs index.
- [ ] It explicitly compares "start from scratch" vs "build on lst".
- [ ] It defines non-goals: no RAG system, no Obsidian clone, no mandatory CRDT/server sync for normal use.
- [ ] It references/reconciles the existing OKF/wiki epic `lst-xadf`.

title: Introduce explicit multi-vault configuration
description:
## What to build

Add explicit multi-vault configuration while preserving backward compatibility with the existing content directory.

Example target shape:

```toml
[[vaults]]
name = "personal"
path = "~/lst"
kind = "notes"
default = true

[[vaults]]
name = "wiki"
path = "~/wiki"
kind = "wiki"
```

## Requirements

- Existing `paths.content_dir` continues to work as the default vault during migration.
- CLI commands can select a vault via flag/config/default.
- Vault paths support XDG/home expansion.
- Vault kinds/profiles are open-ended strings, not hardcoded platforms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Config schema supports `vaults`.
- [ ] Existing single-content-dir config still works.
- [ ] At least note/list commands can resolve the active vault.
- [ ] Tests cover default vault selection and explicit vault selection.

title: Add git-backed vault sync commands
description:
## What to build

Add git-first sync commands for a vault. Git should become the default sync substrate for Markdown vaults.

Potential CLI shape:

```bash
lst sync status --vault wiki
lst sync pull --vault wiki
lst sync save --vault wiki -m "wiki: update notes"
lst sync push --vault wiki
lst sync run --vault wiki -m "..."   # optional pull/save/push wrapper
```

## Requirements

- Commands operate on the selected vault path.
- Detect non-git vaults and report helpful guidance.
- Do not hide merge conflicts; surface git output clearly.
- JSON output supports agents.
- No dependency on `lst-server` or `lst-syncd`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `status`, `pull`, `save/commit`, and `push` are implemented or documented as final command names.
- [ ] Commands have useful human output and `--json` output.
- [ ] Tests cover clean repo, dirty repo, non-git directory, and failing git command.

title: Build fast vault search and find commands
description:
## What to build

Support finding the right information quickly across a selected vault.

Potential CLI shape:

```bash
lst find "karpathy" --vault wiki
lst find --type note "meeting" --vault personal
lst open "raw source policy" --vault wiki
```

## Requirements

- Search Markdown files in the selected vault.
- Prefer simple, fast local mechanisms first: filename/title/frontmatter/body search, fuzzy matching, optional ripgrep integration.
- Output should be useful for humans and agents.
- Avoid building a RAG/vector system in this slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Search returns path, title, snippet/summary where possible.
- [ ] JSON output is available.
- [ ] Fuzzy note/page opening works within a vault.
- [ ] Tests cover title/frontmatter/body matches and ambiguous results.

title: Reframe wiki/OKF support as a vault profile
description:
## What to do

Update the existing wiki/OKF plan so it layers on the new vault model.

## Requirements

- `~/wiki` is a configured vault with kind/profile `wiki`.
- OKF validation is opt-in by level/profile, not imposed on all notes/lists.
- Existing `index.md` and `log.md` conventions are respected.
- Wiki workflow treats pages as compiled synthesis, not raw dumps.
- Raw source policy is documented: small safe text may be checked in; large/private/binary/sensitive/license-risk sources stay outside git with checked-in references/manifests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lst-xadf.1` conventions are updated or superseded to mention vault profiles.
- [ ] `lst wiki lint` or equivalent operates on a vault path/profile.
- [ ] Documentation distinguishes generic vault features from wiki-specific OKF checks.

title: Plan mobile app around local vault plus git sync
description:
## What to do

Define how the Tauri mobile app should work when git is the primary sync substrate.

## Questions to answer

- How does the mobile app clone/open a vault?
- How are credentials handled safely on mobile?
- Is sync manual, background, or both?
- How are merge conflicts displayed and resolved?
- Which commands are provided in UI first: quick note, list add/done, search, sync status?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mobile design note exists.
- [ ] It avoids requiring `lst-server`/CRDT sync for the default path.
- [ ] It defines a minimal first mobile workflow for one git-backed vault.
- [ ] It lists platform constraints and unresolved risks.

title: Deprecate or freeze CRDT/server sync as non-default
description:
## What to do

Create a deprecation/freeze plan for the existing CRDT/server/syncd architecture so it stops driving default product design.

## Requirements

- Inventory affected crates and commands: `lst-syncd`, `lst-server`, `lst-proto`, sync DB/config, auth/server commands.
- Decide whether to keep them experimental, remove them, or leave them as legacy optional components.
- Ensure README and install docs point users to git-backed sync as the default once implemented.
- Avoid breaking useful note/list CLI workflows during the transition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deprecation plan exists in docs or issue comments.
- [ ] User-facing docs stop presenting CRDT/server sync as required for normal multi-device use.
- [ ] Follow-up issues exist for code removal or feature gating if needed.

title: Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling
description:
## Context

We want `~/byteowlz/lst` to become the tooling layer for the shared `~/wiki` workflow. The wiki remains plain Markdown in git, edited primarily from nvim and agents, but should gain an OKF-compatible interoperability layer for validation, export/import, indexing, and future automation.

Reference: Google Cloud blog, "Introducing the Open Knowledge Format" / "How the Open Knowledge Format can improve data sharing" (2026-06-12):
https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/how-the-open-knowledge-format-can-improve-data-sharing

OKF v0.1 concepts to preserve in this work:

- An OKF bundle is a directory of Markdown files.
- Each concept is one file; the file path is the concept identity.
- YAML frontmatter carries a small structured interoperability surface.
- The only required frontmatter field is `type`.
- Common fields include `type`, `title`, `description`, `resource`, `tags`, and `timestamp`.
- Markdown links form the cross-document graph.
- `index.md` is useful for progressive disclosure/navigation.
- `log.md` can be used for chronological history.
- OKF should be treated as a format, not a platform or runtime dependency.

Local wiki policy to preserve:

- Canonical wiki lives at `~/wiki` on each machine.
- Markdown files and git history remain the source of truth.
- Agents must `git pull` before editing, commit coherent changes, and push.
- Avoid schema bureaucracy: scratch/inbox/log material should stay low-friction.
- First-class pages should become OKF-compatible over time.
- Strict OKF export/import should be opt-in, not a blocker for every note.

## Desired outcome

`lst` should provide practical wiki commands that make the shared wiki easier to maintain from nvim, agents, and scripts:

- lint/doctor checks for OKF-compatible Markdown
- pre-commit hook integration
- OKF bundle export/import
- link graph/index support
- clear conventions and examples for `~/wiki`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Child issues exist for conventions, validator/linter, pre-commit integration, export, import, and graph/index support.
- [ ] Each child issue references the OKF ideas it depends on.
- [ ] Work is split into independently grabbable vertical slices.
- [ ] No child issue requires adopting a heavyweight knowledge platform or database before the Markdown/git workflow works.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.

title: Define wiki/OKF conventions for lst
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add project documentation that defines how `lst` treats `~/wiki` as an OKF-compatible Markdown bundle without making OKF strictness mandatory for all notes.

This should document the local policy for nvim/agent workflows and map it to the OKF v0.1 concepts described in Google's Open Knowledge Format announcement:

- Markdown directory as bundle
- one concept per file
- YAML frontmatter as the structured interoperability surface
- `type` as the only required OKF core field for first-class pages
- common fields: `title`, `description`, `resource`, `tags`, `timestamp`
- Markdown links as graph edges
- `index.md` for navigation/progressive disclosure
- `log.md` for chronological history

The conventions should explicitly distinguish loose capture from exportable knowledge:

- Level 0: scratch/inbox/log files, frontmatter optional
- Level 1: normal first-class wiki pages, OKF-compatible frontmatter expected
- Level 2: strict OKF-exportable bundle, frontmatter and links validated

Include examples for likely wiki document types:

- `project`
- `guide`
- `reference`
- `tool`
- `infrastructure`
- `person`
- `runbook`
- `decision`
- `index`
- `log`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documentation explains the OKF-compatible subset `lst` supports and links to the Google Cloud OKF article.
- [ ] Documentation clearly states that the canonical wiki remains Markdown in git at `~/wiki`.
- [ ] Documentation defines Level 0/1/2 validation strictness.
- [ ] Documentation includes copy-pastable YAML frontmatter examples using `type`, `title`, `description`, `resource`, `tags`, and `timestamp`.
- [ ] Documentation explains how nvim users and agents should create/edit pages without relying on Obsidian.
- [ ] Documentation warns against over-enforcing metadata on scratch notes.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.

title: Add wiki lint command for OKF-compatible Markdown
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add an `lst` command that validates a wiki directory for OKF-compatible Markdown conventions. The command should work against `~/wiki` by default, while allowing an explicit path for tests and other bundles.

The first version should be mechanical and boring, not an AI quality reviewer. It should validate the small OKF interoperability surface described in the Google Cloud OKF article:

- Markdown files are concept documents.
- YAML frontmatter is the structured metadata block.
- `type` is the minimal required field for first-class OKF-compatible pages.
- `tags`, if present, must be a list.
- `timestamp`, if present, must be ISO-8601/RFC3339-compatible.
- Markdown links should resolve within the bundle when they point to local files.
- Reserved/navigation filenames such as `index.md` and `log.md` should be recognized.

The command should support at least two modes:

- default/warn mode for day-to-day wiki use
- strict mode for OKF-exportable bundles

Example shape, final CLI naming may vary if it fits existing `lst` better:

```bash
lst wiki lint ~/wiki
lst wiki lint --strict ~/wiki
lst wiki doctor
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Command validates YAML frontmatter parse errors and reports file paths/line numbers where possible.
- [ ] Command checks that Level 1/2 pages have a `type` field according to the documented convention.
- [ ] Command validates `tags` shape when present.
- [ ] Command validates `timestamp` shape when present.
- [ ] Command detects broken relative Markdown links.
- [ ] Command recognizes but does not necessarily fail on Obsidian-style wikilinks unless strict mode requests OKF exportability.
- [ ] Command has `--json` output suitable for agents and pre-commit hooks.
- [ ] Command exits non-zero for parse errors and strict-mode violations.
- [ ] Tests cover valid pages, missing type, invalid YAML, invalid tags, invalid timestamp, broken links, `index.md`, and `log.md`.

## Blocked by

Define wiki/OKF conventions for lst

title: Add pre-commit hook support for wiki linting
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add support for installing and running a git pre-commit hook that uses the new `lst` wiki lint command against staged Markdown changes in `~/wiki`.

The hook should preserve the low-friction wiki workflow. It should block only on problems that are likely to break tools or exports, and warn on advisory issues. This follows the OKF principle that the value is in a simple format, not a heavyweight platform.

Expected behavior:

- In normal mode, block invalid YAML frontmatter and clearly broken local links in first-class paths.
- Warn, but do not initially block, missing optional fields such as `description`, `resource`, and `timestamp`.
- Warn on Obsidian-style wikilinks when the file is in an OKF-exportable path or strict config.
- Allow scratch/inbox/log areas to remain loose according to configuration.
- Provide an install command and documentation.

Example shape, final CLI naming may vary:

```bash
lst wiki hooks install --repo ~/wiki
lst wiki hooks run --staged --repo ~/wiki
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] There is a documented way to install the hook into a wiki git repository.
- [ ] Hook runs only against staged Markdown files when invoked from pre-commit.
- [ ] Hook supports the same `--json`/machine-readable diagnostics path as the linter or wraps it predictably.
- [ ] Hook does not require Obsidian and works for nvim/git users.
- [ ] Hook behavior is configurable enough to keep Level 0 scratch notes non-blocking.
- [ ] Hook has tests or a fixture script that demonstrates pass, warn, and fail cases.
- [ ] Documentation explains recommended first rollout: warn-first, then strict only for exportable bundles.

## Blocked by

Add wiki lint command for OKF-compatible Markdown

title: Implement OKF export from wiki directories
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add an export path that turns a wiki subtree into an OKF-style bundle. The goal is to make `~/wiki` portable to other agents, visualizers, search indexes, or external tools without changing the canonical Markdown/git workflow.

The exporter should follow the OKF design from the Google Cloud announcement:

- output is just files and Markdown
- concept identity is the relative file path
- structured fields live in YAML frontmatter
- cross-document relationships are Markdown links
- no SDK, database, cloud account, or runtime should be required to read the result

The exporter should support strict validation before export and produce a clear manifest or summary for humans and agents.

Example shape, final CLI naming may vary:

```bash
lst wiki export ~/wiki --out dist/wiki-okf
lst wiki export ~/wiki/projects --strict --tar dist/projects-okf.tar.gz
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export command copies or materializes a Markdown directory bundle without requiring a service.
- [ ] Export preserves relative paths as concept identities.
- [ ] Export preserves YAML frontmatter fields: `type`, `title`, `description`, `resource`, `tags`, `timestamp`, plus unknown extension fields.
- [ ] Export can run strict validation and fail before writing an invalid bundle.
- [ ] Export reports bundle summary: files exported, warnings, broken/skipped links, and strictness level.
- [ ] Export can optionally produce an archive suitable for transfer.
- [ ] Tests cover exporting a small fixture wiki with links, `index.md`, `log.md`, and custom fields.

## Blocked by

Add wiki lint command for OKF-compatible Markdown

title: Implement OKF import/merge into the wiki
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add an import path that can ingest an OKF-style Markdown bundle into a wiki directory while protecting existing local notes and git history.

This should allow `lst` to consume bundles produced by other agents or tools using the OKF pattern described in the Google Cloud article:

- bundle is a directory of Markdown files
- one concept per file
- YAML frontmatter carries `type` and common fields
- Markdown links connect concepts

Import must be conservative. The wiki is a human/agent-edited git repo, so overwrites should be explicit and reviewable.

Desired behavior:

- dry-run by default or available as a first-class mode
- report creates, updates, conflicts, and skipped files
- preserve unknown frontmatter fields
- optionally map incoming paths under a namespace/prefix
- avoid silently replacing local edits
- work well with git diffs and review

Example shape, final CLI naming may vary:

```bash
lst wiki import ./incoming-okf --into ~/wiki/reference/imports/vendor-x --dry-run
lst wiki import ./incoming-okf --into ~/wiki --strategy prompt
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Import command reads a directory of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
- [ ] Import validates the incoming bundle before writing, using the wiki linter where practical.
- [ ] Import supports dry-run output showing creates, updates, conflicts, and skips.
- [ ] Import preserves unknown frontmatter fields instead of normalizing them away.
- [ ] Import can place content under a target prefix to avoid path identity collisions.
- [ ] Import refuses or clearly marks conflicts rather than silently overwriting local content.
- [ ] Tests cover clean import, invalid frontmatter, path collision, unknown fields, and namespace/prefix import.

## Blocked by

Add wiki lint command for OKF-compatible Markdown
Implement OKF export from wiki directories

title: Build wiki graph and index support from OKF metadata
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add commands that derive useful navigation/index data from the wiki's OKF-compatible Markdown files. This should make the wiki more usable from nvim, scripts, and agents without requiring Obsidian.

Use OKF-aligned primitives:

- file path is the concept identity
- YAML frontmatter fields provide queryable metadata
- Markdown links form graph edges
- `index.md` files provide human/agent entry points

Initial outputs can be simple and file-based:

- list pages by `type`
- list pages by `tag`
- show backlinks for a file
- detect orphan pages
- generate or update folder `index.md` pages from frontmatter summaries
- optionally emit JSON graph data for future visualizers

Example shape, final CLI naming may vary:

```bash
lst wiki graph ~/wiki --json
lst wiki backlinks ~/wiki/projects/foo.md
lst wiki index generate ~/wiki/projects
lst wiki list --type project --tag rust
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Command can parse wiki files and emit a JSON graph of nodes and Markdown-link edges.
- [ ] Nodes include path identity and available frontmatter fields.
- [ ] Command can list backlinks for a selected page.
- [ ] Command can identify orphan pages or pages with no inbound links.
- [ ] Command can generate or update an `index.md` for a folder using `title` and `description` where available.
- [ ] Generated indexes remain readable Markdown and do not require a service.
- [ ] Tests cover graph extraction, backlinks, orphan detection, tags/types, and index generation.

## Blocked by

Define wiki/OKF conventions for lst
Add wiki lint command for OKF-compatible Markdown

title: Add wiki configuration for paths and validation levels
description:
## Parent

Shape lst into OKF-compatible wiki tooling

## What to build

Add configuration support for wiki tooling so `lst` can know where the canonical wiki lives and which paths should be linted loosely or strictly.

This should follow the repo's existing desktop/CLI configuration expectations:

- command-line arguments override config
- config file overrides environment defaults
- XDG config path should be supported
- provide schema for config validation/LSP completion where appropriate

Configuration should cover at least:

- default wiki root, usually `~/wiki`
- path rules for Level 0 loose areas, Level 1 OKF-compatible pages, and Level 2 strict/exportable bundles
- accepted or recommended `type` values, without hard-closing the vocabulary by default
- whether wikilinks are allowed, warned, or rejected in strict mode
- pre-commit hook behavior

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lst` wiki commands can discover a default wiki root from config, env, or CLI args.
- [ ] Config supports path-based validation levels for loose/normal/strict wiki areas.
- [ ] Config supports advisory `type` vocabularies without requiring a closed enum by default.
- [ ] Config can control wikilink handling policy.
- [ ] Config schema/docs are updated for the new wiki settings.
- [ ] Tests cover config precedence for CLI path, env/config default, and path-level matching.

## Blocked by

Define wiki/OKF conventions for lst
